page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top centre above the text. Main text in one block of verse and short headed epigrams, with the right edge of the scan cut off; no margin notes. Page number or signature at the bottom right corner.

l.i: Quod quacunque venis, fuga est, Carine,
Tam parvo tantam gestes quum corpore
barbam, Non Validi barbam, Validum sed dixero barbam.

main_text.l: Et proprios vitent fœmina virque lares.

l.i: Solus in urbe manes, atque id, mi Posthume, iure:
Nam quocunque venis, quid, nisi pestis,
adest? Quid si corripiat te pestis in urbe morantem?
Nempe etiam pesti, Posthume, pestis eris.

page.notes: The right side of the scan is cut off, so the line endings of several verses are lost and were read from context where possible. Some words are uncertain in the Greek epigram headings and the first line of the page; the text is transcribed as far as legible. The page carries a small printed mark at the lower right which is not text.
